sources.title: قرار وزير الصحة والسكان رقم 44 لسنة 2026 بشأن استبدال الجداول الملحقة بالقانون رقم 182 لسنة 1960 (Minister of Health and Population Decree No. 44 of 2026 replacing the tables annexed to Law No. 182 of 1960 on combating narcotics and regulating their use and trafficking), with the tables attached to it
sources.publisher: Ministry of Health and Population (وزارة الصحة والسكان); Official Gazette supplement al-Waqa'i' al-Misriyya (الوقائع المصرية), No. 39 (continued) (C), 17 February 2026, printed pp. 2-35; copy posted by the Egyptian Drug Authority (هيئة الدواء المصرية)
sources.version: Issued 17/2/2026, in force from publication (Art. 2). Art. 1 replaces all the tables annexed to Law No. 182 of 1960 with the tables attached to the decree. Amended by Decree No. 242 of 2026 (next source). The attached tables (printed pp. 4-35) are scanned images with no text layer, so WebFetch cannot read them
sources.how: WebFetch. The decree text (printed pp. 2-3) was read twice and compared by script: identical apart from format. The table pages 4-35 were probed four times, the last time page by page: each page holds only the masthead and its page number, so no table entry could be read

sources.version: Issued 20/7/2026, in force from the day after publication (Art. 2). Art. 1 replaces the text of item (12) of Table (1), Part One (B), of the tables attached to Decree No. 44 of 2026. The new text of item (12) (printed p. 11) is a scanned image with no text layer
sources.how: WebFetch, read twice and compared by script: identical (1,157 characters with spaces removed). Both readings find no text after the colon of Art. 1, and p. 11 holds only the masthead

sources.title: قرار رئيس هيئة الدواء المصرية رقم (375) لسنة 2026 (Egyptian Drug Authority Chairman's Decree No. 375 of 2026 on the import, tracking of circulation, export and dispensing of 'المواد التي قد يساء استخدامها', substances that may be misused)
sources.publisher: Egyptian Drug Authority; al-Waqa'i' al-Misriyya No. 139 bis (A), 29 June 2026
sources.version: Dated 28/6/2026; published 29 June 2026; in force from the day after publication (Art. 4). Its preamble cites the pharmacy law (Law No. 127 of 1955), Law No. 151 of 2019 and other texts, not Law No. 182 of 1960. Art. 2 requires a regulatory guide, posted on the Authority's website, with an annexed table of the substances concerned
sources.how: WebFetch, three readings: two summaries (the summarizer refused a full verbatim copy) and one verbatim reading of the preamble and the opening of Art. 1; they agree. Used only to identify the annex below as a pharmacy-law list separate from the narcotics tables

unsettled: NO ROWS RECORDED, because the current official tables could not be read online. Egypt's controlled substances are listed in the tables annexed to Law No. 182 of 1960. Ministry of Health and Population Decree No. 44 of 2026 (al-Waqa'i' al-Misriyya No. 39 (continued) (C), 17 Feb 2026) replaced all of those tables (Art. 1), and Decree No. 242 of 2026 (al-Waqa'i' al-Misriyya No. 179, 17 Aug 2026) amended them. The only official copies found online, the Egyptian Drug Authority's PDFs of the two Gazette issues, print the tables as scanned images with no text layer (Decree 44, printed pp. 4-35; Decree 242, p. 11). WebFetch cannot read images, and the brief allows no browser and no shell download. So no list entry was read, no item was matched, and nothing was guessed.

All 77 items are unread, so none is recorded as 'not found' (not_found is empty). By drug page: 2c-x (2C-B, 2C-I, 2C-E, 2C-C, 2C-T-7); 5-meo-dmt (5-MeO-DMT); amphetamine (amfetamine, dexamfetamine, lisdexamfetamine); benzodiazepines (diazepam, alprazolam, clonazepam, lorazepam, bromazepam, etizolam, flualprazolam, flubromazolam); cannabis (cannabis and cannabis resin, delta-9-THC (dronabinol), CBD); cocaine (cocaine, coca leaf); dmt-ayahuasca (DMT; ayahuasca, if named); dxm (dextromethorphan); fentanyl-and-analogues (fentanyl, carfentanil, acetylfentanyl, furanylfentanyl, sufentanil, remifentanil); ghb-gbl (GHB, GBL, 1,4-butanediol); heroin (heroin); ketamine (ketamine, esketamine); kratom (Mitragyna speciosa, mitragynine, 7-hydroxymitragynine); lsd (LSD); mdma (MDMA, MDA, MDEA); mescaline (mescaline; peyote or San Pedro, if named); methadone-buprenorphine (methadone, buprenorphine); methamphetamine (methamphetamine); methylphenidate (methylphenidate); pcp (PCP); prescription-opioids (morphine, oxycodone, hydrocodone, codeine, tramadol, tapentadol); psilocybin (psilocybin, psilocin); salvia-divinorum (Salvia divinorum, salvinorin A); synthetic-cannabinoids (JWH-018, AM-2201, 5F-MDMB-PINACA, MDMB-4en-PINACA, ADB-BUTINACA); synthetic-cathinones (cathinone, cathine, mephedrone, MDPV, alpha-PVP, 3-MMC, 3-CMC, 4-CMC, NEP, 2-MMC, 4-BMC).

Decree No. 242 of 2026 replaces item (12) of Table (1), Part One (B) (printed 'البند (12) الوارد بالجدول رقم (1) - القسم الأول (ب)'). Which substance that item concerns is not legible, because the new text is on the scanned p. 11. This cross-reference is the only fact about the tables' layout that could be read: there is a Table (1) with a Part One (B) that has an item (12).

Earlier texts not used. Decree No. 44 of 2026 replaced all the tables. In its preamble it cites the Supreme Constitutional Court judgment in case No. (33) of judicial year 47 (Constitutional), session of 16/2/2026; the judgment itself was not read. Searches for the tables also return earlier Egyptian Drug Authority decrees (for example 4/2020, 442/2021, 480/2021, 481/2021, 272/2022, 697/2022, 586/2023). These were not opened, because any tables they set or amended are no longer the current ones. A private legal database (manshurat.org) appears in search results for these decrees. It is not an official source, so it was not opened and no fact was taken from it. News reports (Ahram, Masrawy, Maspero, Al Arabiya, Daily News Egypt, Mada Masr and others) and the Cairo Governorate's English news item (read once; it links to no document) were used only to learn that a ruling and a replacement decree existed.

A second, separate official list was read, and it changes nothing. This is the Egyptian Drug Authority's annex of products and substances with misuse potential, issued under the Authority Chairman's Decree No. 375 of 2026, which cites the pharmacy law (Law No. 127 of 1955) and not Law No. 182 of 1960. Its product table names only eszopiclone, gabapentin (also gabapentin enacarbil), cyclopentolate (in some products with phenylephrine), tropicamide and clozapine, so none of the 77 items appears. Because it is not the narcotics tables, its silence cannot show that any item is uncontrolled, and no row was made from it.

To settle (editor's decision): the scanned tables need a reading that WebFetch cannot give. That means either an OCR or browser reading of the Drug Authority's PDF of Decree 44 of 2026 (printed pp. 4-35) and of Decree 242 of 2026 (printed p. 11), which is outside this brief's rules, or a human reading of those 33 pages. Until then Egypt has no national rows. The drug pages keep only the UN treaty layer, and no existing Egypt row is changed: the merge script reads this file as 0 rows on 0 drug pages.
